courses.subject: UGFH
courses.title: In Dialogue with Humanity
courses.description:
The course invites students to investigate the problem of "humanity"—i.e., what it means to be human—at two levels: human as an individual and human as a social being. Students will be engaged in a dialogue with literary writers, philosophers and social reformers who address three fundamental questions: What is it that makes a "good" life for me? What is it that makes a "good" society for everyone? How do I make possible such a "good" life and "good" society?

Students are expected to read, discuss, and write about a wide range of texts extracted from influential classics
of Eastern and Western traditions. They will be encouraged to discover their own answers to the three questions by considering views and arguments expressed in the texts, and by exploring how far and in what ways those views and arguments remain relevant to the contemporary world. Through these learning activities, students develop confidence and competence in engaging with primary texts and relating thoughts expressed in classics to their own lives.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken UGFH1000 or 1001
courses.course_syllabus:
Six texts will be selected from the following eight texts, with at least one text from each theme below:

Theme I: Self and Human Capacity

* The Odyssey
* Symposium
* The Analects

Theme II: Faith and Human Limitation

* The Heart Sutra
* Bible

Theme III: Self in Social Institutions

* The Social Contract
* Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844
* Mind, Language and Society

courses.required_readings:
1. Homer. *The Odyssey* (excerpts of books 1, 2, 5, 16, 19, and 23)
Homer. *The Odyssey*, translated by Stanley Lombardo. Hackett Publishing Company, 2000.

1. Plato. *The Symposium
Plato. *Symposium and The Death of Socrates*, translated by Tom Griffith. Wordsworth Editions Limited, 1997.*

1. Confucius. The Analects (“Xueer”〈學而〉, “Yanyuan”〈顔淵〉)
錢穆，《論語新解》，財團法人素書樓文教基金會・蘭臺出版社，2000。
* The Analects of Confucius*, translated by Burton Watson. Columbia University Press, 2007.

1. *The Heart Sutra* (and Thich Nhat Hanh. *The Heart of Understanding*)
一行禪師，《初戀三摩地》，明潔、明堯譯，橡樹林文化出版社，2016。
Thich Nhat Hanh. *Awakening of the heart essential Buddhist Sutras and commentaries*, Parallax Press, 2012.

1. *The Bible* (*Genesis* 1-4, 11, *The Gospel according to Mark*)
創世紀：《聖經》香港思高聖經學會；馬可福音：《聖經·新約全書，新漢語譯本（註釋版）》漢語聖經協會
* New Revised Standard Version Bible*, National Council of the Churches of Christ in the United States of America,1989.

1. Jean-Jacques Rousseau. *The Social Contract.* (excerpts of books 1 and 2)
Jean-Jacques Rousseau. *The Basic Political Writings* (second Edition), translated and edited by Donald A. Cress. Hackett, 2012.

1. Karl Marx, *Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844* (“Wages”, “Estranged Labor”).
Karl Marx, Early Writings, translated by Rodney Livingstone and Gregor Benton. Penguin Books, 1995.

1. John Searle. *Mind, Language and Society* (Chapters 5 and 6)
* Mind, Language and Society*, Basic Books, 1998.
